performance.pon-rx-power: -10 to -27 dBm (leaflet, page 2, printed as "GPON Rx")
performance.pon-tx-power: 4 to 9 dBm (leaflet, page 2, printed as "GPON Tx")

power.power-input: 100 to 240 V AC, 50 to 60 Hz, the power adapter (Quick Installation Guide, page 9)

gaps.note: The leaflet (page 2) prints "172 x 115 x 40mm (W x D x H)", which the chassis carries. The Quick Installation Guide (page 9) prints "L x W x H: 112mm x 162mm x 42mm". The two share neither a length nor a height. The photographs show a top face about 1.5 times as long as it is wide, which fits 172 / 115 = 1.50 better than 162 / 112 = 1.45, but the top face stands above the ruler in them and the scale is not the ruler's, so they do not settle it.
gaps.wanted: The unit measured with a rule or calliper, or the maker's mechanical drawing.

gaps.note: Three figures for one 12 V DC input. The leaflet (page 2, Power Supply) prints "DC +12V / 1.0A", which the jack carries as `current-max-a`. The Quick Installation Guide (page 9, "Whole-device power supply") prints "12V DC / 2A". The unit's own rating label (IMG_2095, IMG_2096, dated 2022.12) prints "12V" and "1.5A". The voltage agrees in all three.
gaps.wanted: Which of 1.0 A, 1.5 A and 2 A is the rating of the adapter shipped with a current unit.

gaps.note: Operating humidity is "10% - 95% (non-condensing)" in the leaflet (page 2) and "10%~90% (non-condensing)" in the Quick Installation Guide (page 9). Neither is carried.
gaps.wanted: The maker's answer, or the later of the two documents confirmed as current.

gaps.note: The only side face photographed is the right one (IMG_2097, IMG_2098). The left face is drawn as ribs alone and no screw is claimed on it.
gaps.wanted: A photograph of the left face, square on, with a rule beside it.

gaps.note: IMG_2097 shows the right face with a solid band at each end (about 16 mm at the front end and 15 mm at the rear end, where the screws are), the slots only in a middle band, and ribs that run out to the lower edge. The face is drawn as ribs from end to end, which the photograph does not show. The slot and rib sizes are not read here.
gaps.wanted: A square-on photograph of the right face with a rule beside it, to draw the bands, slots and ribs.

gaps.note: IMG_2099 shows both telephone jacks in a grey housing. common/rj11-jack@1 has no finish field, so the drawing keeps the part's own colour; changing it is an edit to a part many devices place.
gaps.wanted: A finish field on the telephone jack, once the colour is checked against a second device.

bottom-layout.note: hand-tuned by owner against the physical unit (Inkscape round-trip of the compiled SVG, 2026-08-15)

chassis.note: datasheet (Dimension WxDxH 172 x 115 x 40mm; DC +12V/1.0A). Mount `desktop`: the reference front and rear views show the box standing on four corner feet with its LEDs on the top face.

dc-in-rating.note: datasheet (DC +12V/1.0A): the `input-voltage` and `current-max-a` of the dc-in jack. The datasheet states no barrel size; the jack is the library's one nominal `dc-barrel`.

environment.note: datasheet - operating 0 to 45 C is printed in both the leaflet (page 2, Hardware Specification) and the guide (page 9); storage -20 to 70 C only in the leaflet. Humidity is not carried because the two differ (see the gap).

jack-finish.note: photo-measured (IMG_2099, the rear face, and the guide's Fig. 2 on page 5, agree): the LAN jack's housing is yellow plastic and the 10G jack's is black. The yellow is the median of the yellow pixels of the LAN jack in IMG_2099, #ccb339, taken under a warm light (the white body reads #d2ccbf in the same frame), so it is the photograph's yellow and not a maker's colour code. The black is the library's own #2b2f33 for a black jack.

physical.note: datasheet - the Quick Installation Guide, page 9, prints "<500g" and no figure the leaflet repeats. A bound is not a weight, so it is carried as a note and `weight-kg` is not stated.

pon-caption.note: the white plastic underside carries NO printing beside the fibre bay (IMG_2095, IMG_2096). PON SC/APC was therefore never silkscreen: it is the modeller naming a part, and silkscreen[] means ink on the moulding. It is now a region, which is what this project has for author annotation, so the drawing no longer claims the vendor printed something it did not

rear-layout.note: photo-measured (stock rear photo, labels ON/OFF POWER 10G LAN RESET TEL2 TEL1)

rear-pon-caption.note: estimated - IMG_2099 shows "PON" printed on the rear face beside the fibre-bay notch, below ON/OFF. Place read off the photograph at the face's own scale (172 mm is 810 px), about 2 mm good; the size is the other rear captions'. The underside carries no such print (IMG_2095).

side-screws.note: estimated - IMG_2097 and IMG_2098 (the same face twice) show a cross-head screw near each end of the right face, one at the rear end near the top edge and one at the front end near the bottom edge, a diagonal pair. Places read off IMG_2097 at the face's own scale (115 mm is 880 px): centres 107.8 mm from the front and 7.4 mm down, and 8.5 mm from the front and 31.0 mm down, each good to about 2 mm. The head is about 5 mm across by the same scale. The left face is not photographed, so none is drawn there (see the gap).
